seoDescription: Discover the power of combining Shadcn/ui with Next.js 13 in this comprehensive guide. Learn how to quickly install and configure Shadcn, add reusable components like buttons and inputs into your project using its CLI, and master theming capabilities. This tutorial walks you through setting up custom color palettes, implementing dark mode with `next-themes`, and leveraging CSS variables for a fully customizable design. See a practical example of building a form with Zod for validation and `react-hook-form`.

chapters.description: An overview of what Shadcn/ui is and what will be covered in the video, including components, theming, and dark mode in Next.js 13.

chapters.title: Initializing Shadcn in Next.js 13
chapters.description: This chapter walks through initializing Shadcn/ui in a Next.js 13 project using the CLI and explains each configuration prompt.

chapters.title: Setting Up a Navigation Component
chapters.description: The video demonstrates how to create a basic navigation component and integrate it into the main page layout.

chapters.title: Adding Shadcn Buttons and Styling
chapters.description: Learn how to add a button component using the Shadcn CLI, import it into your page, and apply basic layout styling with Tailwind CSS.

chapters.title: Understanding Shadcn Theming
chapters.description: This chapter explains how Shadcn theming works using CSS variables for colors like primary and muted, and shows the theme customizer.

chapters.title: Implementing Dark Mode with Next-Themes
chapters.description: Follow this guide to install and configure the `next-themes` package to add a dark mode toggle to the application.

chapters.title: How Theming and Dark Mode Interact
chapters.description: This section explains how Shadcn's CSS variables defined in global CSS automatically handle color changes between light and dark modes.

chapters.title: Building a Form with Zod and React Hook Form
chapters.description: Learn to build a validated form by combining Shadcn's form components with React Hook Form for state management and Zod for schema validation.

chapters.title: Final Thoughts and Recap
chapters.description: The video concludes with a summary of Shadcn's benefits, highlighting its ease of use for adding components, styling, and creating themes.

summary:
## Getting Started with Shadcn/ui

To begin, initialize Shadcn/ui in your Next.js project:

```bash
npx shadcn-ui@latest init
```

During initialization, you'll be prompted to make several configuration choices:

- **Framework**: TypeScript is recommended.
- **Style**: Choose between `Default` and `New York`.
- **Base Color**: `Slate` is the default, but others are available.
- **CSS Variables**: Select **Yes** to enable theming and dark mode.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you are using TypeScript in your Next.js project, you must manually change the path for the Tailwind config file from `tailwind.config.js` to **`tailwind.config.ts`** during the CLI setup.

## Adding and Using Components

Components are not installed as a typical package. Instead, you use the CLI to add the source code for each component directly into your project.

- **Add a component**: `npx shadcn-ui@latest add button`
- **Location**: Components are added to a `components/ui` directory by default.
- **Usage**: Import the component from its local path and use it like any other React component:
  ```jsx
  import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

  <Button>Learn More</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Enroll Now</Button>
  ```

## Theming and Styling

Shadcn/ui's theming system is built on **CSS Variables**, which are defined in your `globals.css` file. This makes it easy to customize your application's look and feel.

- **Centralized Colors**: Variables like `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, and `--muted-foreground` control your app's color scheme.
- **Theme Customizer**: The [Shadcn/ui website](https://ui.shadcn.com/themes) has a theme customizer that generates the CSS variables for different color palettes.
- **Applying a New Theme**: To change your app's theme, simply copy the code from the customizer and replace the corresponding CSS variables in your `globals.css` file.

## Implementing Dark Mode

Dark mode is managed using the **`next-themes`** package.

1.  **Install the package**: `npm install next-themes`
2.  **Create a Provider**: Create a `ThemeProvider` component (code available in the `next-themes` and Shadcn/ui docs).
3.  **Wrap Your App**: In your root `layout.tsx`, wrap your `children` with the `ThemeProvider`.

> [!TIP]
> Configure the `ThemeProvider` to enable class-based toggling and set a default theme:
> ```jsx
> <ThemeProvider
>   attribute="class"
>   defaultTheme="system"
>   enableSystem
> >
>   {children}
> </ThemeProvider>
> ```
4.  **Add a Toggle**: Use the Shadcn CLI to add the `dropdown-menu` component, then copy the pre-built `ModeToggle` component from the docs to easily switch between light, dark, and system themes.

## Building Forms

Shadcn/ui provides components that integrate seamlessly with **React Hook Form** for state management and **Zod** for validation.

- **Dependencies**: Install `react-hook-form`, `zod`, and the Shadcn `form` and `input` components.
- **Schema Definition**: Create a validation schema using `zod.object()` to define fields, types, and validation rules (e.g., `z.string().min(2)`).
- **Type Inference**: Zod's `infer` feature allows you to create a TypeScript type directly from your schema, ensuring type safety.
- **Integration**: The `<Form>` component from Shadcn/ui is designed to work with the `useForm` hook, providing render props to easily build fields with labels, controls, and error messages.
